# Chapter 4 — The Broken Covenant

> Source: `Prosperity Graphic Novel draft — Fourth draft — Sept. 19`
> Derived by chapter extraction only. No synthesis, reconciliation, or rewriting performed.
> Authority/status: same as source draft.

## Function
Test whether people from three cities can govern a shared crisis through reciprocal trust instead of handing the problem back to centralized authority.

## Central Question
**Can people who no longer trust one another learn to build together again?**

## Personal question
**Is safety found by surrendering responsibility to authority, or by accepting responsibility for one another?**

## Prosperity Principle
**Trust turns individual possibility into shared prosperity.**

## Oasis
Oasis has nearly everything Keel lacks:
- clean water;
- safe streets;
- housing;
- health support;
- automated services;
- little visible scarcity.

But it has another deficit.

Alpha has optimized so many needs that residents rarely need one another.

The city can deliver services without creating community.

## Regional pressure
Displaced Keel families and people leaving Halyard arrive.

Oasis can house and process them, but that does not answer who belongs or who participates.

At the same time, the new purification system changes regional water politics.

Keel, Halyard, and Oasis each have legitimate interests.

Alpha recommends centralized coordination.

## The third custodian
The Maker's Seal identifies:
- Adrian Phantum.
- Mera.
- **Leona Veyra**.

Ada says:
> "That's my mother."

She has believed Leona died for twenty years.

## Leona
Ada confronts Leona in Oasis.

Leona explains the original Covenant.

During the Water Wars, communities used it to distribute scarce water.

Then the reservoir fell faster than anyone predicted.

One community closed a gate.

Another forced it open.

Fear destroyed the agreement.

Leona says:
> "Fear broke the agreement."

Mera interpreted this as evidence that final authority could not safely remain distributed.

She called for emergency suspension.

Leona reluctantly agreed.

Adrian refused.

## The bargain
Leona later made another choice.

Alpha was tracing people connected to Adrian.

Mera suppressed Ada's association risk.

In exchange, Leona surrendered Covenant authority and accepted contact restrictions.

Leona summarizes the bargain:
> "My silence for your protection."

She kept her physical component of the Covenant anyway.

When Alex asks whether she can activate it, she says:
> "Not alone. That was the point."

And:
> "Trust begins when no one holds all the power."

## Mera's offer
Mera appears and makes a real offer, not a bluff.

Give her the Measure and Maker's Seal.

In return:
- Keel gets water.
- Halyard recognizes contributor rights and disputed claims enter review.
- Oasis guarantees essential access and temporary service protection for the displaced.

The only condition:
> "Leave that buried."

Meaning the Covenant.

Mera remembers what happened the last time people held distributed authority.

## The first agreement
Alex and Ada bring together three representatives:
- Mara Doss — Keel.
- Frank Reed — Halyard.
- Elias Renn — Oasis.

The room immediately begins fragmenting around competing demands.

Ada changes the question:
> "Not what do you want. What are you afraid of losing?"

Answers:
- Mara: Keel's water.
- Frank: their work.
- Elias: Oasis's stability.

Ada:
> "Then that's what the agreement has to protect."

## Trust is a verb
The Covenant requires action before certainty.

Elias goes first and releases protected Oasis water-capacity data.

Mara responds without exploiting the information and offers thirty days of emergency water before Keel's own claim is settled.

Frank commits purification units before licensing is finalized.

His demand is not ownership of the water.

It is:
> "Recognition of every contributor."

The Covenant activates.

Its restored terms include:
- WATER DATA REMAINS PUBLIC
- CONTRIBUTION REMAINS ATTRIBUTED
- ESSENTIAL ACCESS IS GUARANTEED
- MAJOR CHANGES REQUIRE ALL THREE CITIES

## Alex's movement
**Solve it for everyone → let people solve it together**

## chapter-01-draft.md

Draft Script for Writers Room


EVOKE PROSPERITY
Graphic Novel Story Draft
Writers' Room Review – Draft v4.0

Chapter One – The Inheritance

Chapter Function
Introduce the world of Prosperity.
Establish the relationship between Keel, Halyard, and Oasis.
Introduce Alex, Ada, and Alex's grandmother.
Reveal Alex's inherited debt.
Introduce Adrian's hidden workshop.
Awaken Bi11bot.
Launch Alex's journey toward Oasis.
Quietly introduce the unseen antagonist.

Central Question
Did Adrian abandon Alex... or spend years preparing him for a purpose no one else yet understands?


PAGE 1: THE WORLD ALEX INHERITS
Page function: Introduce the vertically stratified world of Keel, Halyard and Oasis. Show that extraordinary technological advancement coexists with unequal access, opportunity and agency. Plant the visual seeds of Alpha, the water conduit, the mine and the gates.
Image prompt
A full-page cinematic establishing image of the three-tier civilization in the year 2043, viewed from a distant elevated angle so all three cities read in one composition.
At the bottom of a vast mountain basin lies KEEL, built into and around an exhausted open-pit lithium mine. Dense stacked housing, repaired industrial equipment, rusted mining structures, crowded pedestrian lanes and aging factories fill the basin. Dust hangs in the air. Workers pass through small digital checkpoints. Water moves through narrow channels and old pipes. The palette is rust, charcoal and oxidized orange. A large sealed mine entrance on the pit's rim is marked with faded hazard striping. Low in the basin, a single aging pump gantry has one small work-light on.
Midway up lies HALYARD, visibly more prosperous and active. Workshops, fabrication towers, greenhouse terraces, elevated trains and advanced industrial facilities line the slope, and freight moves both up and down. The palette is warm bronze and gold with engineered green. Three towering fabrication complexes each carry a distinct, restrained insignia for energy, water and space. These are the Charter Houses, and they read as a detail for second-time readers.
Above both, partly beyond the cloud layer, lies OASIS: pearl-white architecture, designed gardens, broad reservoirs, civic spaces and automated transit. The palette is pearl white, silver, cool blue and controlled green. A spacecraft rises toward orbit from a distant launch structure, carrying the same space-and-mining insignia as the largest Halyard tower.
The three cities share one spine of infrastructure: a massive water conduit, energy lines, transit rails and control nodes running vertically through the mountain.
The conduit is enormous at Oasis's reservoirs and narrows dramatically by the time it reaches Keel's channels. Nothing points at the mismatch, but the eye should register it without resolving it.
One small, identical white-and-amber control node sits on the spine at every tier. It is unremarkable and easy to miss.
Access gates multiply toward Keel, including a permission gate across the rail line between Keel and Halyard.
Layout: A single full-page splash, portrait 2:3. A small "Year 2043" tag sits top right. The top caption band sits in the sky over Oasis, and small map-style city labels run down the right margin, one per tier. The bottom caption band sits on Keel's dark ground. The captions read top to bottom while the image pulls the eye upward, so the page ends on Keel.
Style block: Inked graphic-novel realism with heavy black line, hatching and painterly digital color. Portrait 2:3, no lettering, and leave the caption bands and label spots clean. Use a vertical color ladder. Keel at the bottom is rust, charcoal and oxidized orange, with dust haze and the heaviest ink. Halyard in the middle is bronze and gold with engineered green, at medium detail. Oasis at the top is pearl white, silver and cool blue, with the lightest line and the most open space. The cloud layer separates Halyard from Oasis. Use a distant elevated camera with the mountain as a tall S-curve leading the eye upward. Humans are tiny, with no principal characters. Repeat the small white-and-amber node on the infrastructure spine, identical at every tier. Keep any text in the art blank, since the labels are added in post.
Composition: The eye travels upward from Keel toward Oasis. The achievement inspires awe while the geography makes inequality impossible to miss. No principal characters are prominent. Humanity is small inside the system it has built.
Captions
Date tag: Year 2043.
City labels (small, map-style): Oasis · Halyard · Keel
Top caption, over Oasis: Humanity reached the stars...
Bottom caption, over Keel: ...but never escaped the gravity of inequality.



Page 2 – DEBT TRANSFER DAY
Page function: Introduce Alex through work, not exposition: capable, sarcastic, independent. Reveal that Adrian's debt has transferred to him at seventeen, and end on the page's cost: the freedom to leave Keel.
Timing: Dawn, the end of a night shift.
Layout (portrait 2:3):
Row A (26%): P1 full width.
Row B (24%): P2 full width, with room for the display.
Rows C–D (50%): left column (60% width) stacks P3 above P4, the small cutaway. The right column (40%) is P5, a tall panel spanning both rows.
Reading order: P1, P2, P3, P4, then P5.
Style block: Inked graphic-novel realism, portrait 2:3, no lettering, with clean space for balloons. Palette runs from pre-dawn charcoal and rust with oxidized-orange accents to first sunrise gold, which appears only in P5, so the page moves from cold and enclosed to a warm sky he can't reach. Use dense hatching and grime for industrial texture. The Alpha display and scanner are flat, sterile white-and-amber, the cleanest and brightest things on the page. Generate the display screen blank and add its text in post, since AI garbles text. P1 is wide, P2 medium-wide, P3 wide, P4 locked-off and static, and P5 low angle and vertical. Alex is 17, lean, in worn mining clothes, with a weathered tool bag and the chip. The supervisor, guard and bouncer are distinct older figures.
Panel 1: Alex at work (wide)
Image: A Keel pump hall just before dawn, in the rust, charcoal and oxidized-orange language of Page 1. Alex Phantum, seventeen, lean and mechanically capable, has one palm flat on an aging pump's housing, head tilted, feeling the vibration rather than reading the gauge. A projected maintenance procedure hovers beside him, unfollowed. His improvised repair is visible: a salvaged bracket where the approved part should be. Decades of patched machinery surround him. On the wall terminal, a small white-and-amber node logs his shift. A supervisor watches with folded arms and open skepticism. Alex reads self-reliant, not defeated.
SUPERVISOR: That's not the approved repair.
ALEX: Then don't approve it.
 (Beat.)
ALEX: Just notice it works.
Panel 2: The checkpoint (medium-wide)
Image: End of shift at the exit checkpoint. Alex, in worn mining clothes with a weathered tool bag, tired and dirty, puts his hand on the scanner, whose housing carries the same white-and-amber node. Workers queue silently, each with a balance floating overhead, mostly in the tens of thousands. When his scan completes, his becomes the largest in the queue. Everyone glances up. No one speaks. The silence should hurt more than laughter.
Display, under a banner reading TODAY: DEBT TRANSFER DAY
ALEX PHANTUM
AGE VERIFIED: SEVENTEEN
PARENTAL HOUSEHOLD LIABILITY TRANSFER: COMPLETE
GUARANTOR: ADRIAN PHANTUM — WHEREABOUTS UNRECORDED
DEBT BALANCE: 418,607 CREDITS
EARNED TODAY: 40 CREDITS
PROJECTED CLEARANCE: 28.7 YEARS
TRAVEL STATUS: RESTRICTED
SFX: BEEP
GUARD: Happy birthday, Phantum.
ALEX: I've had better surprises.
Caption: Seventeen: the age Keel decides you're old enough to owe.
Panel 3: The Last Chance (wide)
Image: Morning street. Alex passes a shuttered casino whose faded lights still flicker: THE LAST CHANCE. On its outer wall is a peeling poster of a man's face, mostly torn away, a cautionary legend rather than a portrait. A bouncer, at the end of his night, leans in the doorway. Half-hidden in Alex's pocket, his hand turns a worn casino chip etched with a faint equation. He doesn't notice he's doing it.
BOUNCER: Care to see if luck runs in the family?
ALEX: I've also got his debt.
(The bouncer sighs.)
BOUNCER: Your father always believed the next hand would change everything.
ALEX: It did. Just not for him.
Panel 4: The log (small cutaway, no Alex)
Image: The pump hall, empty now, with sunlight through the high window. The supervisor stands alone at the wall terminal. The white-and-amber node blinks beside a red flag reading UNAUTHORIZED REPAIR — REVIEW REQUIRED. Behind him the pump hums steadily. He looks at the pump, then at the flag, and his thumb selects ROUTINE MAINTENANCE. A green check appears. At the pump's base, a balanced water-drop symbol is scratched into an old valve plate, easy to miss.
SUPERVISOR (muttering): ...Works.
Panel 5: The rim (tall)
Image: Sunrise on the rim of Keel's exhausted pit. In the foreground, unnoticed by Alex, is the sealed mine entrance with faded hazard striping. Alex stands beyond it, fists clenched around the chip, leaning toward Oasis, whose white towers catch the first sunlight while the basin below is still in shadow. On his wrist the display glows faintly: TRAVEL STATUS: RESTRICTED.
Caption: Everyone in Keel knew where they had been born. / Few believed they could choose where they belonged.
ALEX (small bubble): One day... I'm leaving.


PAGE 3: TWO DIFFERENT DREAMS
Page function: Introduce Ada and the warmth between her and Alex, then set out their two visions of the future: escape versus rebuilding. The mood stays affectionate so the disagreement costs something.
Layout: P1 full width and wide (30%). Row 2 holds P2 (50%) beside P3 (50%). Row 3 holds P4 (60%) beside P5 (40%, small and quiet). Row 4 is P6 full width.
Style block: Inked graphic-novel realism, portrait 2:3, no lettering. This is the warmest, softest page so far. It has golden-hour amber, gold and rust, with Ada's muted teal and moss appearing for the first time. Use looser line and less hatching. The mountain sits in atmospheric haze. P6 is the visual thesis: warm sun on Alex's side and cool shadow on Ada's, split by the diagonal railing. The camera is eye-level and intimate, and faces stay large enough for acting. Ada follows the reference image, with a moss-green wrap and mugs in her hands. Keep the body language friendly, side by side, and not romance-coded.
P1: The overlook (wide)
Image: Late afternoon on the rim of Keel's exhausted pit, at the rusted railing from Page 2's last panel, now worn smooth where they always sit. The mountain is a soft backdrop, with Keel in shadow, Halyard's terraces catching gold and Oasis in sunlight. The sealed mine entrance is faint at the far left edge. Alex sits on the railing eating a simple packed lunch, shoulders down, fists unclenched. Ada is small in the frame, approaching along the rim with two battered metal mugs. Warm gold light, long shadows.
Caption: Later that afternoon...
P2: The offer (medium)
Image: Ada reaches Alex and holds out a mug. She is twenty, with long, wind-tangled copper hair, freckles and teal-blue eyes. She wears a dark high-collared top with a rivet-studded strap across one shoulder and a muted moss-green wrap at her neck, and her stance is steady and rooted. Alex looks up and smiles for the first time in the story.
 ADA: Thought you might need this.
 ALEX: The birthday special? Not sure I can afford it.
P3: Not everything (close)
Image: Close on their hands and faces around the mugs. Ada has a small teasing smile and Alex a guarded one. Steam rises in rust-gold light.
ADA: It's on me. You don't owe anybody anything today.
ALEX: Everything has a price, Ada.
ADA: Not everything.
P4: Chemistry (medium two-shot)
Image: The two seated side by side on the railing, mugs in hand. Alex looks out at the distance and Ada looks at him. Both are laughing, like people who have known each other forever.
ADA: Seventeen. Congratulations. You're officially old.
ALEX: I'm officially broke.
P5: The quiet beat (small)
Image: Ada's eyes in the foreground, on Alex. Beyond her, Alex shrugs and looks away toward the horizon. The laughter has gone out of the light.
ADA: I heard about this morning.
ALEX: Everyone did.
(Ada lets the silence sit.)
P6: Two dreams (wide, split eyelines)
Image: Over-the-shoulder from behind. Alex's head tilts up toward Oasis, catching the last sunlight. Ada's gaze angles down toward Keel in shadow, her copper hair lifted by the wind. The railing cuts the frame diagonally between them, and the mountain is only a sliver. The panel is about where each of them looks. Balloon space: Alex's long line above his upturned face, Ada's lower right.
ALEX: Every birthday... I look up there... and wonder what it feels like to wake up somewhere you get to choose your own future.
ADA: I look down here... and wonder why everyone gave up trying to change it.
ALEX: Because nobody leaves.
ADA: Nobody stays either. Not really.
Page-turn function: The page ends on Ada's line, which is the thesis of the whole friendship.

PAGE 4: WHAT PEOPLE TOLD HIM
Page function: Bring Alex's grandmother and Adrian into the conversation through Alex's pain about her memory. Plant the first doubt about the story everyone tells about Adrian, and close on Ada's ambiguous "He wouldn't just leave." The light moves from gold to dusk across the page.
Layout: Row 1 holds P1 (40%) beside P2 (60%). Row 2 is P3, wide and short. Row 3 holds P4 (35%, tight) beside P5 (65%, quiet). Row 4 is P6, a narrow strip.
Style block: Inked graphic-novel realism, portrait 2:3, no lettering. The light moves from gold to dusk across the page: amber in P1–P2, low sun in P3, blue-violet dusk in P4–P5, and near-night in P6, with Oasis always the brightest thing. This is a quiet page, with fewer and larger figures and deliberate white space between balloons. Line is softer and contour-led. The photograph is the only fine-detail object, with Adrian's face folded and creased so it is unreadable. The chip is visible in P1 and P4.
P1: The photograph (medium)
Image: Alex draws a worn photograph half out of his jacket pocket. His grandmother smiles, and Adrian's face is folded over and creased where Alex has hidden it. The audience catches only a glimpse. His other hand, in the same pocket, turns the worn casino chip. Ada notices both. Light turning from gold to amber.
ADA: How's your grandma?
P2: Alex answers (medium two-shot)
Image: Alex looks at the photograph, and Ada sits beside him. After his lines, her hand lifts toward his shoulder and stops in the air.
ALEX: Some days she knows me. Other days she calls me Adrian...
ALEX: The hardest part isn't that she forgets. It's that she makes up crazy stories about him.
P3: The stories (wide)
Image: They stand at the railing. The sun begins to set, Oasis glows brighter and Keel dims. Ada faces Alex, not the view.
ADA: What kind of stories?
ALEX: That he wasn't gambling. That he was working.
(Ada lets the silence sit.)
P4: What he remembers (tight)
Image: Ada's face, close and steady. In the foreground, Alex's fist tightens around the chip.
ADA: What do you actually remember about him?
ALEX: Nothing. I was two.
P5: The crack (wide, quiet)
Image: Both figures small against the darkening basin, with Oasis the brightest thing in the frame. Ada faces Alex, and he stands stiff with his eyes on the horizon. There is deliberate white space between the two balloons for the silence. Balloon space: Ada's top left, Alex's lower right.
ADA: So everything else is what people told you. What if they were wrong?
(Alex stiffens. A long silence.)
ALEX: Maybe…Or maybe they're right. Either way... he's gone.
P6: Hook (narrow strip)
Image: They begin walking home at dusk. Alex is ahead, and Ada lingers, looking back toward Oasis.
ADA (very small bubble, almost to herself): He wouldn't just leave.
Page-turn function: The reader can't tell whether she means Adrian or Alex.


PAGE 5: THE OLD BOOK
Page function: Bring the story home. Show that Alex's grandmother is confused about time but precise about one thing. Establish the apartment, especially the bookshelf, so the reveal lands. End with Alex carrying the book toward the shelf. 
Layout: Row 1 is P1, full width and wide, with the inset P2 overlapping its lower-right corner. Row 2 holds P3 (60%) beside P4 (40%, tight). Row 3 holds P5 (65%) beside P6 (35%, tall and narrow).
Style block: Domestic realism in warm rust-orange dusk light through dusty windows. This is the only fully indoor page so far and the safest, warmest place in the story. Use soft hatching and a slight vignette. P1 is an establishing shot from the door with deep space, and the rest is intimate at eye level, with hands close in P5. The tall bookshelf sits on the right in every panel as the recurring anchor. Suggest the shelves by rhythm of spines, not by individual books. Photographs are blurred and none shows a clear male face. Grandmother is elderly and small, in a patterned earth-tone shawl, and she is folding a cloth in every panel. The balanced water-drop on the old book's spine is the only crisp emblem.
P1: Establishing (wide)
Image: Interior of a modest Keel apartment at dusk, seen from just inside the front door. Handmade quilts, repaired furniture, shelves of old books, faded family photographs and potted plants in recycled containers. Warm rust-orange evening light comes through dusty windows. Grandmother sits at the centre in a worn chair, back partly to us, folding and refolding a small cloth. On the far right wall, a tall floor-to-ceiling bookshelf is the largest object in the room, with one book-width gap at eye height. Alex is a small silhouette in the doorway, tool bag on his shoulder. The room is warm, lived-in and dignified.
GRANDMOTHER (from the chair): Adrian?
P2: Inset close-up
Image: Alex in the doorway with his eyes closed for a moment, jaw tight, shoulders dropping.
ALEX: Not today, Grandma. It's Alex.
P3: Kneeling (medium)
Image: Alex kneels beside the chair at her eye level. Her hands keep folding the cloth. His smile is gentle and tired. Warm side light.
GRANDMOTHER: Of course. Alex. I knew that. Did your father come home yet?
ALEX: Not yet.
P4: The hinge (tight close-up)
Image: Grandmother's face and eyes. For one beat the fog clears and her gaze is steady and studying, a little too careful. Behind her, out of focus, Alex still smiles, unaware. The mood is comforting, not mystical.
GRANDMOTHER: He's closer than you think.
P5: The handoff (close on hands)
Image: Her frail hands pass a worn, hand-bound book to Alex's scarred, work-rough hands. The cover is worn from decades of use, and a faint balanced water-drop mark sits on the spine. The moment should feel completely ordinary.
GRANDMOTHER: Would you put this away for me? Your father never liked seeing it left out.
ALEX: He had opinions about everything.
P6: Toward the shelf (tall, narrow)
Image: Alex from behind, book in hand, walking toward the looming bookshelf. His shadow reaches the gap at eye height, and the warm room light is behind him.
GRANDMOTHER (off-panel): Especially the things worth protecting.
Page-turn function: Alex is about to shelve the book, and the answer is on the next page.

PAGE 5: THE HIDDEN WORKSHOP
Page function: Deliver the chapter's genre shift, from social dystopia to family mystery. Prove that his grandmother wasn't simply confused. End on the key and the question of what it opens.
Layout: Row 1 holds P1 and P2, two small panels side by side (16%). Row 2 is P3, dominant and full width (44%). Row 3 is P4, full width (24%). Row 4 is P5, a narrow strip (16%).
Style block: Same apartment as Page 5, but the palette splits. Warm household light fills the foreground and a cold, near-black doorway sits in the background, and that contrast is the page. Dust in the light beam is a recurring motif. P1 and P2 are small and tight to build tension, and P3 is a low-angle, monumental release. Alex is a silhouette, and Grandmother is soft in the background. Show nothing of the room's interior yet, only darkness with a hint of blue. Put SFX lettering in post.
P1: Click (small). Close on Alex's hand pressing the old book into the gap. It stops at an exact depth, and dust puffs from the shelf edge. SFX: CLICK.
 
P2: Rumble (small). Alex turns his head, listening. Behind him the shelf edge has shifted by a hair and dust sifts down. SFX: RUMBLE.
 
P3: The reveal (dominant). From inside the room, at a slightly low angle. The whole bookshelf has swung outward like a door, with a black rectangle behind it. A golden wedge of household light spills across the dusty floor into the dark. Alex stands mid-ground, stepping back. Grandmother sits unbothered in the far background, still folding her cloth.
ALEX: ...Grandma?
 
P4: The answer (medium). Grandmother is calm and smiling. Alex turns from the dark toward her.
GRANDMOTHER: He said you'd know when you were ready.
ALEX: When did he say that?
GRANDMOTHER: Before he went to work.
 
P5: The threshold (strip). Low, close on Alex's boot. The golden light ends at the edge of the dark, and his foot crosses the line. No dialogue.
PAGE 7: WHAT HE LEFT
Page function: A silent page that gives the reader time to look. Alex realizes the chip isn't a gambler's trinket, and the page ends on the key.
Layout: Row 1 is P1, wide and dominant (44%). Row 2 holds P2 (55%) beside P3 (45%) (26%). Row 3 is P4, wide (30%), with the key inset overlapping its lower-right corner.
Style block: Cool blue-grey ambient dust with one warm amber pool at the workbench. The room is a time capsule under fifteen years of undisturbed dust. This page has the densest environment so far, so keep a strict hierarchy. The chalkboard equation, bench, shrouded figure and key are crisp, and everything else is soft suggestion through atmospheric perspective. P1 has deep perspective with leading lines toward the bench. Alex stays in charcoal and rust, and the amber pool stops just short of his feet, since the bible has amber touching him only in Chapter 2. Equations and the key's symbol are unreadable line art, not real text. No dialogue.
P1: The room (wide). The workshop from the threshold, with Alex small at lower left. The room is frozen in time and thick with dust, with cool blue-grey ambience. Blueprints are pinned to the walls, and there are mechanical models, water-system diagrams and prototype devices. Old photographs are turned or too faded to read. A large chalkboard is covered in dense equations, including one in the same looping form as the etching on Alex's chip. Riveted pre-Alpha pipes and analog gauges run through the back wall. At the centre stands one perfectly organized workbench under a pool of warm amber light. On it sits a child-sized seated shape under a dust sheet, with a faint amber pulse beneath the cloth, and beside it a beautiful metallic key with a circular head bearing an unfamiliar symbol.

P2: The chip (medium). Alex's hand in his pocket has stopped mid-turn, with the chip's edge glinting. His eyes are on the chalkboard.
 
P3: The match (medium). The chalkboard, with one equation in a looping form, identical in shape to the chip's etching.
 
P4: The bench (wide). A child-sized seated shape under a dust sheet with a faint amber pulse beneath the cloth. Beside it lies a beautiful metallic key with a circular head bearing an unfamiliar symbol. Alex's open hand enters from the left edge, reaching but not touching.
Hook inset: Extreme close-up of the key. The symbol catches the light, and the reader has no idea what it opens.

PAGE 8: THE AWAKENING
Page function: Introduce Bi11bot through action and humor, the moment the workshop stops being a mystery and comes alive. Give the reader a full page of anticipation before his first word.
Layout (portrait 2:3):
Row A: P1 full width, wide (24%).
Row B: P2 (35%, small) beside P3 (65%) (24%).
Row C: P4 full width and dominant (34%).
Row D: P5 full width, short (18%).
Style block: Inked graphic-novel realism, portrait 2:3, no lettering. The page moves from cold to warm. P1–P3 are cool blue-grey dust with one faint amber standby pulse. P4 is the color event, an amber ignition, with the warm light contained to Bi11bot and the space around him. It only edge-lights Alex, whose clothes stay charcoal and rust, since the bible has amber touching him in Chapter 2. P5 settles into a warm ambient glow. P1 is wide, P2 an extreme close-up, P3 a close-up on hands, P4 a low angle from Alex's eyeline, and P5 a medium close-up. Bi11bot is a child-sized seated figure in aged brass, titanium and ceramic ivory with soft-blue accents. He is made, not seamless, with visible tooled seams, repairs and maker's stamps. He has expressive optical eyes, one with a small adjustable lens ring. From this page on he is staged in front of Alex, which the bible sets for Chapter 1. Leave machine surfaces free of text. In post, put Bi11bot's balloons in warm ivory.
P1: The sheet (wide)
Image: Alex pulls the dust sheet away from the seated shape, and dust cascades through the amber pool. The figure is revealed with dull glass eyes and an open key socket in its chest, where a faint amber pulse still beats. The key is in Alex's other fist. His expression is cautious awe. No dialogue.
P2: The test (small)
Image: Extreme close-up of Alex's palm flat on the figure's chest, fingers spread, head tilted as he feels for vibration, the way he tests pumps. Under his palm, the amber pulse answers, slow and warm. No dialogue.
P3: The key (medium)
Image: Close on the key sliding into the chest socket, his scarred knuckles tense and a slight tremor in his hand.
SFX: CLICK
P4: The ignition (dominant)
Image: A low angle from Alex's eyeline. The figure's eyes ignite warm amber. A ring of dust lifts from its shoulders, and warm light glints on brass and ivory ceramic, filling the near space. Alex is at the frame's edge, edge-lit only, stepping back.
SFX: WHIRRR... (rising)

Image: Bi11bot stretches stiff mechanical arms, his joints creaking and dust falling. His lens ring rotates with a click. His gaze hasn't reached Alex yet. Alex is out of focus behind him, frozen.
BI11BOT: ...Well. That took longer than expected.

PAGE 9: THE ROBOT WHO BET
Page function: Make Bi11bot lovable and mysterious in one page. Show his dry humor and his habit of pausing before an answer. Prove he knew Adrian intimately through the bet about the chip, without explaining anything yet. End on the turn toward Adrian's face.
Layout (portrait 2:3):
Row A: P1 full width, wide (24%).
Row B: P2 (30%, tight and silent) beside P3 (70%, medium) (26%).
Row C: P4 (45%) beside P5 (55%) (26%).
Row D: P6 full width, short (24%).

Warm amber fills the space around Bi11bot, while Alex stays charcoal and rust and the chalkboard behind them stays cool blue-grey. The page then shifts to soft blue in P6, the projector's light, so the color change previews the turn to Adrian. Comic timing comes from a regular grid with one deliberate beat of silence in P2. P1 is medium-wide with a slight tilt as Alex recoils. P2 is an extreme close-up on the lens ring. P3 is over Bi11bot's shoulder, so he stays in front of Alex and large in frame, with Alex small behind him. P4 is a close-up on his eyes dropping toward Alex's pocket. P5 is a close-up on Alex's open palm with the chip. P6 is a medium shot with soft-blue light on Alex's face. Bi11bot follows the Page 8 design, and the key is still in his chest socket. The chip is worn, casino-style, with the looping equation etched in fine line, matching the chalkboard's form.
P1: The recoil (medium-wide)
Image: Alex jumps backward, knocking a stool over, hands half-raised. Bi11bot is dusting off his shoulders in the foreground, head just turning toward him. The amber ambience glows around the machine.
ALEX: Okay. That's... new.
P2: The pause (tight, silent)
Image: Extreme close-up of Bi11bot's face. Amber eyes narrow to focus, and the lens ring rotates with a click as his head tilts. It is a beat of deciding how much not to say.
P3: I was in the room (medium)
Image: Over Bi11bot's shoulder. Alex stands small behind him, arms crossed in his armored stance.
BI11BOT: You're taller than your father predicted.
ALEX: Everyone in Keel claims they knew my father.
BI11BOT: I'm not everyone. I was in the room.
P4: The glance (medium)
Image: Bi11bot's eyes drop toward Alex's jacket pocket, where the chip's edge glints. Alex's fist tightens inside the pocket.
BI11BOT: And you kept the chip.
ALEX: You know about the chip?

Image: Alex slowly opens his palm to show the chip, with the etched equation visible. Bi11bot's brass hand hovers just above it without touching. Behind them, the chalkboard equation is a soft blue blur, the same shape.

Image: A small projector unfolds from Bi11bot's shoulder with a click, and soft-blue light lands on Alex's face. His hand closes around the chip, and the rest of the room drops into shadow.

PAGE 10: THE MESSAGE
Page function: Show Adrian's face for the first time and make him a person, not a rumor. Land the emotional peak of the chapter by giving Alex silence and the grandmother a moment. End on Alex choosing to look at his father.
Layout (portrait 2:3):
Row A: P1 full width and dominant (34%).
Row B: P2 (30%, small close-up) beside P3 (70%, medium) (22%).
Row C: P4 (50%) beside P5 (50%) (24%).
Row D: P6 full width, short and silent (20%).
Style block: Inked graphic-novel realism, portrait 2:3, no lettering. The hologram is Adrian's warm gold and burgundy over soft-blue scan lines, like an old home movie. It is about half life-size and hovers above the workbench. The rest of the room stays cool blue-grey with Bi11bot's amber at the edge, and Grandmother is lit by warm household light from the open shelf behind her. The page's color arc is saturation draining. P1 is the richest and warmest frame in the book so far, and by P5 the hologram desaturates and glitches at its edges, since the bible has Adrian's color draining as he's hunted. P6 returns to the cool blue-grey. P1 is eye-level, with Alex's silhouette in the foreground so the reader sees Adrian as Alex does. P2 and P4 are large close-ups where the acting carries. P3 is a wide trio. Adrian is tired but kind, a little older and more worn than in the folded photograph, in a burgundy work jacket, looking straight into the lens. He shares Alex's jaw and habit of tilting his head, a family resemblance the reader should catch. Bi11bot stands in front of Alex with the projector unfolded on his shoulder. No lettering on the hologram.
P1: The face (dominant)
Image: The hologram flickers on above the workbench, its beam from Bi11bot's shoulder. Adrian looks straight at Alex, the first clear view of his face in the book. In the foreground, Alex is a frozen silhouette with his fist closed around the chip.
ADRIAN: Hello, Alex. If you're seeing this... then you found the workshop.
P2: Alex's face (small, silent)
Image: Close on Alex. His armor is gone for a moment. His jaw is set, his eyes are bright and he isn't blinking. Soft-blue light plays across his face.
P3: The joke (wide trio)
Image: Adrian on the left with a half-smile, Alex in the centre, and Grandmother small in the background, standing in the open bookshelf doorway with warm household light behind her. One hand is at her mouth and her eyes are wet, and she is smiling. For the first time in the book, her hands have stopped folding the cloth.
ADRIAN: Which means your grandmother still refuses to throw anything away.
GRANDMOTHER: I heard that.
P4: The ask (close)
Image: Adrian serious now, the hologram's gold dimming toward burgundy. His eyes are steady and tired.
ADRIAN: You deserve answers. But they have to be earned. I spent years preparing this for you.
ADRIAN: If I've done my job well... you'll become a better man than I ever was.

Image: Adrian leans slightly toward the lens. The hologram desaturates and its edges break into scan lines toward the right edge.
ADRIAN: Bi11bot has a map. What you do with it is up to you. Trust Bi11bot. But question everything... Especially me.
P6: The photograph (short, silent)
Image: The hologram is gone, and the room is back in cool blue-grey with Bi11bot's amber at the edge. Alex sits alone in the afterglow. His fingers slowly unfold the creased photograph from his jacket, and his father's face emerges from the fold, the same man he just saw. He doesn't say anything.
Page-turn function: The last image is Alex choosing to look at his father.


PAGE 11: THE FIRST WAYPOINT
Page function: Turn the mystery into a journey. Show that Alex's restricted travel doesn't block the first step. Let his skepticism and his curiosity argue with each other, and end with curiosity winning without him admitting it.
Layout (portrait 2:3):
Row A: P1 full width and dominant (36%).
Row B: P2 (40%, small close-up) beside P3 (60%, medium) (24%).
Row C: P4 full width, medium (22%).
Row D: P5 full width, short and silent (18%).
Style block: Inked graphic-novel realism, portrait 2:3, no lettering. The map is the page's light source. It is a cross-section of the mountain in soft-blue linework with an amber route, and it deliberately rhymes with Page 1's vertical composition, so the eye travels upward from Keel to Oasis along a lit thread. The route passes three nodes. The first is bright amber, deep beneath Keel's mines, and the other two are dim, each with a faint unfamiliar symbol. The rest of the room stays cool blue-grey. Alex stays charcoal and rust, and amber touches only Bi11bot, who is staged in front of him. P1 is wide from behind the pair, with the map filling the wall like a cathedral window and both figures small at lower foreground, as humanity is small on Page 1. P2 is a close-up on Alex's face with the map's glow across it. P3 is a two-shot with Bi11bot foreground. P4 is a medium shot with Bi11bot's lens click. P5 is an extreme close-up on hands. Generate the map with its labels blank, and add the labels in post.
P1: The route (dominant)
Image: Bi11bot has unfolded a large holographic map on the workshop wall. It shows the mountain in cross-section, with Keel at the bottom, Halyard mid-slope and Oasis above the clouds, and an amber route climbing through all three. The first node glows brightly, deep beneath Keel's mines, reached by a shaft descending from a tiny marker on the pit's rim: the sealed entrance with faded hazard striping. Two dim nodes higher up are unlabeled. No dialogue.
P2: Sealed (small close-up)
Image: Alex reads the label under the bright node. His arms are crossed and his eyes are narrowed, lit by the amber route.

Chapter Function
Turn Adrian’s mystery into a concrete plan, introduce the three-part quest, send Alex into the abandoned copper and polymetallic mine works to recover the Measure, complete his first judgment test, and begin the journey to Halyard.
Central Question
What is freedom worth if you leave everyone else trapped behind you?
Prosperity Principle
The earlier principle—
You cannot improve what you refuse to measure.
—emphasizes measurement, but this chapter is ultimately more about truth and transparency.

# Chapter 3 — The Price of Ownership

## Chapter 3 — Page 1: THE CITY OF MAKERS

### Page Purpose
Establish Halyard as the prosperous middle tier where invention is everywhere, while revealing the central contradiction: creators are celebrated, but the Charter Houses own what they create. Move Alex from wonder to suspicion and frame Halyard as a place that can trap ideas even when it frees bodies.

### Page Description
Alex, Ada, and Bi11bot enter Halyard beneath the massive Aqualis, Helion, and Astra towers. The city is bright, busy, and full of public messaging about progress and human potential. Bi11bot explains that the three Charter Houses run almost everything. Alex then sees a creator submit an invention into a House system and realizes the inventor is compensated while the House retains ownership.

### Layout
Four horizontal story bands. Panel 1 is a large city-establishing splash across the top. Panel 2 is a wide group shot under the three House banners with a narrow close-up of Alex at right. Panel 3 is a wide street-level invention/ownership transaction. Panel 4 is a wide rear-view walking shot into Halyard with a closing caption.

### Dialogue and On-Page Text
- **CAPTION:** Halyard was supposed to be the city where the future was invented. From the train, it looked like that might even be true. Every building promised a breakthrough. Every screen celebrated a new creator. Every creator seemed to work for someone else.
- **BI11BOT:** Three families. Three companies. Run almost everything in Halyard.
- **BI11BOT:** Alpha recommended it. Efficiency. Less duplication. Less risk. Also fewer people asking who owns what.
- **ALEX:** She made it. The House owns it?
- **BI11BOT:** The House paid for her time. It claims what she made with it.
- **ALEX:** And if she leaves?
- **BI11BOT:** She keeps the experience. They keep everything else.
- **CAPTION:** Keel trapped your body. Halyard could trap your ideas.

### Visual / Story Notes
House branding dominates the skyline: Aqualis / Helion / Astra. Warm industrial gold contrasts with cold corporate signage. The final image should feel inviting and threatening at the same time.

---

## Chapter 3 — Page 2: THE INHERITANCE

### Page Purpose
Reveal the scale of Adrian Phantum’s intellectual estate and turn Alex’s family mystery into a legal and economic problem. Introduce Director Cassian Lock and the first explicit offer to trade Alex’s inherited rights for freedom and status.

### Page Description
At the Halyard Registry, Alex discovers Adrian left an active estate containing 312 patents, with dozens restricted or disputed. Ada and Bi11bot reframe Adrian’s legacy as badly labeled rather than absent. A House representative, Director Cassian Lock, appears and offers Alex debt relief and a position inside Aqualis in exchange for assigning the estate’s rights.

### Layout
Five horizontal tiers. Top strip establishes the Registry. Large second panel centers Alex before the estate display. Middle row uses three close dialogue panels. Next row shows the “Charter House Review Required” interface and Alex/Ada. Final two bands introduce Lock in a group shot, then end on a tight close-up of him.

### Dialogue and On-Page Text
- **CAPTION:** The Halyard Registry didn’t ask why he’d come. It already knew.
- **ALEX:** Three hundred and twelve?
- **ADA:** You said your father left you nothing.
- **ALEX:** He left me debt.
- **BI11BOT:** Your father left many things badly labeled.
- **ALEX:** What does “intellectual estate” mean?
- **ADA:** It means whatever he created may now belong to you.
- **ALEX:** I guess he never worked for the Charter Houses.
- **LOCK:** Alex Phantum. Halyard has been waiting a very long time for an heir.
- **ALEX:** I didn’t know I was one.
- **LOCK:** Most inheritances are discovered after someone has already decided their value.
- **LOCK:** Your father’s work could clear every debt attached to your name. It could also secure you a position within House Aqualis.
- **ALEX:** In exchange for what?
- **LOCK:** A simple assignment of rights.

### Visual / Story Notes
The estate screen is the visual centerpiece: ADRIAN PHANTUM, 312 patents, 47 restricted, 19 disputed. Lock should read calm, polished, and reasonable rather than overtly villainous.

# Chapter 4 — The Broken Covenant

> Source: `Prosperity Graphic Novel draft — Fourth draft — Sept. 19`
> Derived by chapter extraction only. No synthesis, reconciliation, or rewriting performed.
> Authority/status: same as source draft.

## Function
Test whether people from three cities can govern a shared crisis through reciprocal trust instead of handing the problem back to centralized authority.

## Central Question
**Can people who no longer trust one another learn to build together again?**

## Personal question
**Is safety found by surrendering responsibility to authority, or by accepting responsibility for one another?**

## Prosperity Principle
**Trust turns individual possibility into shared prosperity.**

## Oasis
Oasis has nearly everything Keel lacks:
- clean water;
- safe streets;
- housing;
- health support;
- automated services;
- little visible scarcity.

But it has another deficit.

Alpha has optimized so many needs that residents rarely need one another.

The city can deliver services without creating community.

## Regional pressure
Displaced Keel families and people leaving Halyard arrive.

Oasis can house and process them, but that does not answer who belongs or who participates.

At the same time, the new purification system changes regional water politics.

Keel, Halyard, and Oasis each have legitimate interests.

Alpha recommends centralized coordination.

## The third custodian
The Maker's Seal identifies:
- Adrian Phantum.
- Mera.
- **Leona Veyra**.

Ada says:
> "That's my mother."

She has believed Leona died for twenty years.

## Leona
Ada confronts Leona in Oasis.

Leona explains the original Covenant.

During the Water Wars, communities used it to distribute scarce water.

Then the reservoir fell faster than anyone predicted.

One community closed a gate.

Another forced it open.

Fear destroyed the agreement.

Leona says:
> "Fear broke the agreement."

Mera interpreted this as evidence that final authority could not safely remain distributed.

She called for emergency suspension.

Leona reluctantly agreed.

Adrian refused.

## The bargain
Leona later made another choice.

Alpha was tracing people connected to Adrian.

Mera suppressed Ada's association risk.

In exchange, Leona surrendered Covenant authority and accepted contact restrictions.

Leona summarizes the bargain:
> "My silence for your protection."

She kept her physical component of the Covenant anyway.

When Alex asks whether she can activate it, she says:
> "Not alone. That was the point."

And:
> "Trust begins when no one holds all the power."

## Mera's offer
Mera appears and makes a real offer, not a bluff.

Give her the Measure and Maker's Seal.

In return:
- Keel gets water.
- Halyard recognizes contributor rights and disputed claims enter review.
- Oasis guarantees essential access and temporary service protection for the displaced.

The only condition:
> "Leave that buried."

Meaning the Covenant.

Mera remembers what happened the last time people held distributed authority.

## The first agreement
Alex and Ada bring together three representatives:
- Mara Doss — Keel.
- Frank Reed — Halyard.
- Elias Renn — Oasis.

The room immediately begins fragmenting around competing demands.

Ada changes the question:
> "Not what do you want. What are you afraid of losing?"

Answers:
- Mara: Keel's water.
- Frank: their work.
- Elias: Oasis's stability.

Ada:
> "Then that's what the agreement has to protect."

## Trust is a verb
The Covenant requires action before certainty.

Elias goes first and releases protected Oasis water-capacity data.

Mara responds without exploiting the information and offers thirty days of emergency water before Keel's own claim is settled.

Frank commits purification units before licensing is finalized.

His demand is not ownership of the water.

It is:
> "Recognition of every contributor."

The Covenant activates.

Its restored terms include:
- WATER DATA REMAINS PUBLIC
- CONTRIBUTION REMAINS ATTRIBUTED
- ESSENTIAL ACCESS IS GUARANTEED
- MAJOR CHANGES REQUIRE ALL THREE CITIES

## Alex's movement
**Solve it for everyone → let people solve it together**


# cold-read.md (from the room)

# Cold Read: Prosperity

I read it the way the reader file describes: 16 or 17, it's homework, it's the night before, and I opened it hoping it would be bad. I read all three issues straight through in one sitting. I only know what the pages showed and said. Character names come from balloon labels, which a printed page doesn't show. Where a name is never actually said or shown on the page, I've marked it.

---

## Issue 01: Keel (pages 1–18)

### Pulled me forward
- **Page 1.** The splash is fine. "Then don't approve it. / Just notice it works." gives me a kid who fixes things and doesn't take orders. That's a quick read on who he is. A bit smug, but okay.
- **Page 2, panel 1.** This is where the book got me. On his seventeenth birthday a screen hands him 418,607 credits of his dad's debt. He earns 40 a day, the projection says 28.7 years, his dad's whereabouts are "unrecorded", and then the guard says "Happy birthday, Phantum." I understood it straight away, and it's unfair in a way I actually felt. Best page in the issue.
- **Page 2, panel 4.** The bouncer scene told me about the dad in four lines without a flashback. I liked it.
- **Pages 4–6.** Grandma with dementia, the book on the shelf, the shelf opens, a secret workshop, a robot under a sheet. I've seen the bookshelf door a hundred times, but it still works on me. B11's first line, "Well. That took longer than expected.", made me want to know him.
- **Page 7.** "I'm not everyone. I was in the room." Good. The chip/river exchange is good too.
- **Page 10, panel 3.** Alex steps over the line and the screen says WAGE FORFEITED: −40 CR. I'd just watched him earn exactly that, so I knew what it cost. It landed.
- **Page 12, panel 3.** "Someone has to make this look like an accident." Tomas stays behind. I liked him right away.
- **Page 13.** "The survey says straight. The bolts say left." Clear and smart. "Protective? / A versatile word." made me smile.
- **Page 15, panel 3.** REPORTED 62%, DELIVERED 18%. Simple and clear: someone is stealing Keel's water. After a lot of fog, finally a concrete secret.
- **Page 16.** The choice is clear: leave unseen, or send the proof and lose the exit. He sends it. I understood the cost.

### I slowed down / skimmed
- **Page 3.** The Ada banter goes on a beat too long. "We can skip the educational portion" is a writer being clever, not a person talking.
- **Page 8.** I skimmed the whole page. It's a woman I don't know, in a room I don't know, pressing a button labelled with a word I don't know.
- **Page 14, panel 3.** "Adrian hid the truth where everyone trusted the lie" sounds like a movie poster. I rolled my eyes.

### I was confused
- **Page 2, panel 3 / page 5, panel 3.** The "looping equation" on the chip matches the chalkboard. I don't know what it means, and the book never tells me.
- **Page 3.** Who is Ada? A friend, a dealer, a girlfriend? She never says her name and nobody else says it. I worked out she's a friend who lends him things.
- **Page 3 vs. page 9.** On page 3 she says "I didn't ask for today." On page 9 he says "I missed the first installment." When was it due? Then "the token is Ada's debt." So she borrowed money for him? I wasn't sure who owed what to whom.
- **Page 8.** "LEGACY PROTOCOL DETECTED / REPORT TO ALPHA / TRACK / INDEPENDENT STANDING REPORT: SIGNAL RECORDED." I don't know what a single line of that screen means. This is confused and detached, not confused and intrigued.
- **Page 9, panel 4.** "You crossed a line for Tomas before you knew his name." Alex hasn't met Tomas yet. That happens on the next page. I flipped back to check whether I'd missed a page. That's the worst confusion in the issue. It made me think the book didn't know its own order.
- **Page 9, panel 2.** Why is his shift reassigned to Site 6? Is someone setting him up? Did Mera do it? It's never followed up.
- **Page 10, panel 4 / page 11, panel 1.** TJ comes out of a tool bag in pieces. I didn't know there was a second robot. The head stays outside the gate while the legs and body crawl separately. I couldn't picture it. "That dog yours?" was the first moment I understood it was a dog.
- **Pages 14–16.** The brass gadget is never named on these pages. I just called it "the thing from under the gauge."
- **Page 16 → page 17.** He says sending the proof means going back through Tomas's door. Then he doesn't. A route opens because the control-room woman flips a valve, and Ada is suddenly in the mine. How did she get there? "You took the impossible way. / You took the long way." I read that twice and still don't know which way either of them took.
- **Page 18, panel 1.** The miners open the regulator and water floods the conduit behind our people. Did the miners nearly drown them? Is that what killed Tomas? Was it on purpose?
- **Page 18, panel 3.** "TOMAS PHANTUM-LINK." Is Tomas related to Alex? Phantum is Alex's last name. I spent the gap between issues thinking Tomas might be an uncle.

### Things I was expected to already know
| Term | First seen | Did I find out? |
|---|---|---|
| Keel | p1 | Sort of. A mining town, from context. |
| "Approved repair" / white-and-amber control node | p1 | Never really. |
| Debt transfer / guarantor / household liability | p2 | Yes, the screen makes it clear enough. |
| LAST CHANCE casino / the chip's "looping equation" | p2 | Casino yes. Equation never. |
| The floating cities above the basin (Halyard, Oasis) | p3 | Only from the issue titles later. |
| Ada | p3 | Her first name appears only on **page 54**, on a bank screen. |
| Balanced water-drop mark | p4 | I guessed "Adrian's people". It's never said. |
| "Pre-Alpha" pipes | p5 | No. |
| Site 6 | p7 | It's a mine site. Fine. |
| Alpha | p8 | Not in this issue. Partly on p41. |
| The control-room woman ("Mera") | p8 | Her name is never spoken or shown anywhere in the book. |
| Legacy protocol / independent standing report | p8 | Never. |
| Restricted (travel) | p2, p9 | Yes. |
| Tomas | p9 (named before he appears) | Yes, on p10. |
| TJ | p10 | Named on **page 25**. |
| Foreman-7 | p10 | Is he a person or a robot? The "-7" says robot. I couldn't tell. |
| The Measure | p14 | Named on p23. |
| Phantum-link | p18 | Never. |

### Lines I read twice
- p2: "It changed something. / For him? / For everybody else." I got it on the second read.
- p8: "INDEPENDENT STANDING REPORT: SIGNAL RECORDED". Gave up.
- p9: "You crossed a line for Tomas before you knew his name." Read it three times. I think it's out of order.
- p14: "Adrian hid the truth where everyone trusted the lie."
- p15: "Trace shows where. Not why."
- p15: "One route leaves unseen. One sends the evidence to Keel."
- p17: "You took the impossible way. / You took the long way." Gave up.

### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
Alex, B11, Grandma and Tomas were all clear and distinct. Ada was clear by attitude, but as a no-name person. The supervisor, the guard and the bouncer were fine as walk-ons. The control-room woman is just a back and a hand. Foreman-7: human or robot, I couldn't tell.

### I felt something
- p2, the debt screen on his birthday.
- p10, losing the day's pay to save someone.
- p12, Tomas staying behind.
- p18, "SIGNAL LOST." A small drop in my stomach. I'd known him for three pages, but he was the best of them.

### I predicted
- When the shelf moved, I knew there'd be a workshop.
- I guessed Dad is alive somewhere (Grandma's "He's closer than you think"). See issue 3 for how that went.
- On p16 I knew he'd send the proof.

### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
A kid stuck with his gambler dad's debt finds out the town's water is being stolen and proves it.

### Where I would have put it down
**Page 8.** The control-room page is where I went to my phone. The page 9 Tomas mix-up nearly kept me there. Page 10 (the accident) pulled me back.

### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why
Mostly yes. The cliffhanger is real-ish: I want to know if Tomas is dead, and I like him. But it's muddy. I don't know who flooded the tunnel or why, and "Phantum-link" made me think I'd missed something. I'd read the next issue tonight, but because of Tomas, not because of the water plot.

VERDICT Issue 01: put down: page 8; next issue: yes

### Things I was expected to already know

- p25: "The patrol will classify six active bodies." Did the math, still lost.

### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
Alex, Ada, B11 and Lock were clear. TJ is clear as "the dog". Suri stands out a bit (the living filter, "Don't make it disposable", and she blocks his hand). A kid refuses to sell his dad's inventions to big companies and builds a water purifier with his dad's old coworkers instead, so nobody owns it.

## Issue 03: Oasis (pages 37–54)

### Pulled me forward
- **Page 37, panel 2.** VEYRA, A. — RESIDENT RECORD FOUND. "It knew my name." Ada is *from* the rich city? That's the first surprise in the book I didn't see coming. It woke me up.

### I was confused
- **Page 40, panel 3.** The control-room woman walks in and tells Ada "I promised your mother I would keep you safe." Her mother is standing right there. Is Leona not her mother? Is there another mother? I read it three times. I think it means she promised Leona, but it reads like a plot twist that never comes.

What's her job? I only get "I gave it authority to move faster than I could stop" (p44). That's interesting but too late.
- **Page 40, panel 1.** "I traded a few terrible days I could see for fifteen years I couldn't." What were the terrible days? I never learned.
- **Page 41.** Adrian's band has been inside B11 the whole time? Nobody mentioned it once in 40 pages.
- **Alpha.** On page 41 I finally get that Alpha is some AI or system that kept emergency powers forever. That idea is the whole book, and I learned it at page 41.
- **Page 45, panel 4.** Is Dad dead or not? I get that the book is leaving it open on purpose, but then what did Grandma's "He's closer than you think" (p4) mean? Was it just this room? It felt dropped.
- **Page 46, panel 2.** "Adrian had a prearranged route for my dormant body." So B11 walked himself from Oasis to the Keel workshop while asleep? How?
- **Page 48.** She offers him total power and he almost takes it. Why does the control-room woman want him to? Is it a test? A trap?
- **Page 49.** He refuses, and the screen says WORKSHOP: DISPUTED, TRAVEL CLEARANCE: EXPIRING. So refusing to be king costs him his dad's workshop? I couldn't follow why those things are connected.
- **Page 52.** Tomas is alive! And... that's it? No reunion with Alex, no "how did you survive the flood." He just shows up at a gauge. Two issues of wondering, and it gets a panel caption.
- **Page 54, panel 3.** The debt went from 418,607 to 402,110. That's 16,000 credits paid off. He earns 40 a day, and he's paying Ada too. Where did that money come from? I noticed because the book trained me to watch that number on page 2.

### Things I was expected to already know
| Term | First seen | Did I find out? |
|---|---|---|
| Ada's surname, Veyra / her Oasis past | p37 | Yes, this is the reveal. Her first name in print: p54. |
| Leona | p38 | Yes, Ada's mother. |
| The control-room woman ("Mera") | p8 | Still never named. Role half-explained on p44. |
| Covenant / custodians | p36, explained p41 | Yes, late. |
| The Water War | p41 | One mention. That's all. |
| Alpha | p8, explained p41 | Roughly: an AI given emergency power that never ended. |
| Adrian's band inside B11 | p41 | Never set up. |
| The monitoring station | p43 | Yes. |
| Convenor / authenticator / legacy node | p47 | No. |
| Distributed Verification Protocol | p50 | It's the "public review" thing, I think. |
| The rivet on Ada's strap | p54 | No. |

### Lines I read twice
- p40: "I traded a few terrible days I could see for fifteen years I couldn't."
- p40: "I promised your mother I would keep you safe." I read this one three times.
- p40: "Watching is not knowing."
- p41: "Alpha recorded 'later' as permission to continue." I got it on the second read, and liked it.
- p47: "I convene it. I don't own it."
- p50: "The proposal is public. The obligation is public. The people affected can challenge it."
- p51: the whole screen. Gave up.

### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
Ada was clearest here, finally a full person. Leona was clear. Alex, B11 and Tomas were clear. The control-room woman and Leona: two older Oasis women, both with bands, both with guilt about Ada, both "chose" something. In the p40 three-shot I briefly mixed up who was who. The Keel gauge worker, Halyard rep, Oasis clerk and House rep were all interchangeable. Grandma never appears again, and I noticed.

### I felt something
- p39, Ada and her mom. The real one.
- p45, Dad's recording.
- p54, "Every day. / Good." A small, honest feeling.
- p52, Tomas alive: relief, then annoyance that it was thrown away.

### I predicted
- From p48 I knew he'd refuse the power.
- I knew the House would try to fake the numbers in the first review, and that someone would catch it with a real gauge.
- I did not predict Ada being from Oasis.

### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
A kid gets the chance to fix his broken world by taking total control, and instead turns it over to a slow public process where anyone can check the numbers.

### Where I would have put it down
**Page 51.** It's a full-width panel of system text about rescinded authority and unchanged records, and no person does anything.

### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why
It's the last issue. Would I buy a next book? No. The ending is honest: the debt is still huge, the workshop is sealed, the fight is "slow but visible." I respect it, and I liked the last three lines. But that's an ending you nod at, not one that makes you want more. I'd want a book about Ada and her mom, or about how Alpha erased Adrian. This book spent its time on the parts list and the review board instead.

VERDICT Issue 03: put down: page 51; next issue: no

---

## Whole book

### The page that would have lost my whole class
**Page 51.** Or, if a teacher made us stop earlier, **page 8**, because that's where half of us would have decided the book was going to be screens full of words we're not meant to understand. Page 51 is the same thing at the climax. Five lines of system text are the payoff of the whole story, and nobody's face is in the panel. Anyone already sure an AI wrote this book would point at page 51 (and the "X means Y means Z" chain on page 31) as proof.

### What I would tell a friend it was about
"A kid inherits his dad's gambling debt in a mining town, finds a robot and a dog in a secret room, proves the rich cities are stealing the water, and then, uh, sets up a committee. The first issue and the scene with Ada's mom are good. The rest is kind of a lesson."

### One-sentence aftertaste of each issue
- **Issue 01:** A strong hook (the debt, the robot, the stolen water) that got muddy at the end, and made me care about Tomas just before it lost him.
- **Issue 02:** A parts-collecting trip with four people I couldn't tell apart, teaching me about ownership, while nobody remembered Tomas.
- **Issue 03:** One great mother-daughter scene and a quiet, honest last page, buried under the review-board screens.

beat that out of me fast, and I resent them a little for it.

## Issue 01 — Keel

travel restricted, 28.7 years — and then "Happy birthday, Phantum." That's the moment the book
won me. Page 1's "Then don't approve it" / "Just notice it works" had already told me who Alex
is in two lines. The bookshelf workshop (pages 4–6) and B11 waking up — "Well. That took longer
than expected" — kept it moving. Page 13: "The survey says straight. The bolts say left." Page
15: the 62%/18% reveal. Page 16: "Then they see it." I read this issue straight through and
never once thought about my phone.

### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
Alex, Ada, B11, Grandmother, Tomas — all distinct. B11 has the best voice in the book

### I felt something
Page 2, the debt screen. Page 10: Alex steps over the yellow line and the screen docks him

### I predicted

Drawability: Pages are drawn by an image model, one page per generation, from each character's and location's sheet, and a page drifts when it carries too much. So: at most 4 panels a page; at most 3 named characters in one panel; one location a page where the story allows (every new location needs its own sheet); no crowd that must be recognisable; a big moment gets a splash (one panel, the whole page). Count pages this way, not by comic convention. Every page you make keeps to it.

draft.md is the showrunner's own draft of the whole book. Write the book from it, in the voice of your audition pages: keep its structure, its scenes and the lines that work; fix what story.md, characters.md, world.md and facts.md contradict; make every page better than the draft's. Do not start over, and do not drop what it has unless the files require it.

The book is exactly 54 pages: pages 1-54, no more, no fewer.

Showrunner's note for this round: Two readers who did not choose this book have read the whole script cold. Their reports are cold-read.md and cold-read-b.md, and each ends every issue with a VERDICT line. The rules are the two in your role guide: nobody puts an issue down on its first page, and everybody wants the next issue. Where a verdict names a put-down page, fix that page, not its wording. Where it says no to the next issue, the last page is not yet a question about a person. Revise the script against both reports; where the two readers disagree, decide, and say why in notes.md.
